question: Where should your finished knot sit after tying a simple interrupted stitch?

options.A: Tucked tightly underneath the tissue forceps
options.B: Off to the side of the incision line
options.C: Buried deep underneath the subcutaneous fat layer
options.D: Directly in the center of the open wound gap

explanation: Always pull your knot off to the side! This keeps it from pressing down directly into the healing cut and causing irritation. Perfect technique!

question: Which detail is NOT required when documenting a new peripheral IV insertion?

options.A: The catheter gauge and anatomical location
options.B: The brand name of the soap used for handwashing
options.C: The patient's response and tolerance to the procedure
options.D: The date and exact time of the insertion

explanation: Standard hand hygiene is assumed; charting focuses on the specific procedure details like size, location, time, and patient response. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h10)

question: How long must pain stick around before it is officially called chronic pain?

options.A: Less than 30 days
options.B: Longer than 3 to 6 months
options.C: More than 24 hours
options.D: Exactly one week

explanation: You're doing great! While acute pain heals quickly, chronic pain hangs around long past the normal healing time—usually defined as lasting over 3 to 6 months.

question: What should a nurse do if a medical doctor prescribes an obviously dangerous dose of a controlled drug?

options.A: Question the order and clarify with the prescriber before giving it
options.B: Throw the medication away without telling anyone
options.C: Ask another patient to take the extra dose instead
options.D: Administer the medication anyway since the doctor signed it

explanation: Nurses are legally responsible for the medications they administer and must question unsafe orders. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is the correct technique for pulling out a peripheral IV catheter?

options.A: Twist the hub rapidly while pulling outward with force
options.B: Lift the tip upward quickly at a 90-degree angle
options.C: Flush the line with saline right before pulling it out
options.D: Pull it out smoothly and parallel to the skin surface

explanation: Keep it smooth! Pulling the catheter out parallel to the skin prevents it from scraping or tearing the delicate inside lining of the vein.

question: A patient stumbles when walking and cannot coordinate their finger-to-nose movement during a physical exam. Which brain structure is most likely impaired?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: Inability to perform smooth coordinated movements or maintain balance points directly to cerebellar dysfunction. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient decides to stay in an abusive home for a little longer while sorting out resources. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Collaborate with the patient to create a practical safety plan for the home
options.B: Call the police immediately to force the patient out of the house
options.C: Cancel all future home visits to avoid getting involved
options.D: Tell the patient that continuing to stay is illegal

explanation: Respect the patient's pace! Help them stay as safe as possible right where they are until they feel ready to make their move.

question: What is the main result when a genetic mutation affects a receptor?

options.A: The receptor becomes misshapen, altering normal hormone response
options.B: The hormone itself changes into a dangerous chemical toxin
options.C: The blood supply to the target endocrine gland is cut off
options.D: The cell membrane immediately dissolves into the bloodstream

explanation: A genetic typo changes the building blocks of the receptor protein, making its shape wonky so it doesn't fit the hormone key quite right. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why isn't a simple exam grade enough to judge a nursing student?

options.A: Written exams are illegal in nursing schools
options.B: Clinical tutors just love writing long stories
options.C: Grades don't show real hands-on clinical skills
options.D: University rules ban traditional grading scales

explanation: A letter grade on a paper test can't show how well you insert a cannula or comfort an anxious patient. That's why nursing needs more than just pen-and-paper grades!

question: A family notices that their monthly income stays the same, but the cost of staple foods doubles due to inflation. What is this family most likely forced to do?

options.A: Stop eating entirely without changing any shopping habits
options.B: Invest their remaining savings into local agricultural farming
options.C: Buy cheaper, highly processed foods to stretch their tight budget
options.D: Automatically increase their daily consumption of fresh organic produce

explanation: When purchasing power drops, families must switch to less expensive, often less nutritious food alternatives. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h6)

question: Which term describes an objective and measurable alteration in body function?

options.A: Disease
options.B: Wellness
options.C: Illness
options.D: Continuum

explanation: Disease refers to the pathological changes inside the body that medical tests can measure and detect. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which blood-borne infection has the highest statistical risk of transmission after a single accidental needle-stick?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.C: Hepatitis B virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B is remarkably hardy and infectious. That is why getting your Hep B vaccine and safety training early in nursing school is so important!

question: Why must nurses strictly follow the doctor's weight-bearing orders during mobility training?

options.A: To prevent the client from building too much muscle too quickly
options.B: To protect healing bones and surgical repairs from excessive stress
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing mobility equipment
options.D: To ensure the client does not burn an excessive number of calories

explanation: Spot on! Putting too much weight on a healing bone or fresh surgery too soon can mess up the repair and cause setbacks.

question: Why do we take a baseline assessment when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: It helps the nurse detect small changes in the patient's condition over time.
options.B: It replaces the need to review previous medical history charts.
options.C: It eliminates the need to perform further physical examinations during the shift.
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will experience a rapid recovery.

explanation: Spot on! A baseline is your starting point. Knowing where your patient starts helps you easily spot if they are getting better or worse during your shift.

question: What exactly is a chemical hazard?

options.A: Only industrial gases released into the atmosphere
options.B: Biological agents that cause infectious diseases
options.C: Prescription medications administered strictly by a physician
options.D: Any chemical that can cause harm to health or the environment

explanation: You've got this! A chemical hazard is simply any substance or mixture that has the potential to cause harm to people, property, or our environment. Think of everyday harsh cleaners or lab chemicals.

question: What happens when a manager tries to set too many objectives at the same time?

options.A: Staff members get spread too thin and miss targets.
options.B: Every objective gets achieved much faster.
options.C: Employees experience a sharp decrease in stress.
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores automatically double.

explanation: Trying to do everything at once usually means nothing gets done well. It's always better to focus on a few key priorities!

question: Why should you always involve community members when assessing their own health needs?

options.A: It relieves the ministry of health from paying salaries to community nurses
options.B: It eliminates the need to collect data using formal questionnaires
options.C: It proves that the community does not need any external medical help
options.D: It builds local ownership and commitment to solving the identified problems

explanation: When people help discover the problem, they take pride in fixing it. Involving them turns a project from 'your idea' into 'our community goal!'

question: As a nurse, you'll hear about SBAR. What does this acronym stand for?

options.A: Shift, Bed, Analysis, Report
options.B: System, Blood, Assessment, Reaction
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Basic, Action, Review

explanation: Spot on! SBAR is your best friend for quick, clear handovers and phone calls with doctors. It helps you state the Situation, give the Background, share your Assessment, and state your Recommendation.

question: Which antibiotic is commonly prescribed first-line for animal and human bite injuries?

options.A: Erythromycin ointment
options.B: Ciprofloxacin drops
options.C: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
options.D: Vancomycin syrup

explanation: Amoxicillin-clavulanate is a great choice because it covers the wide variety of bacteria typically found lurking in human and animal mouths.

question: How can strict cultural rules about modesty affect how women use healthcare services?

options.A: They eliminate the need for nurses to take a thorough patient history
options.B: They may prevent women from seeing male practitioners, delaying necessary care
options.C: They guarantee that women receive priority treatment in private clinics
options.D: They automatically improve health outcomes by reducing community exposure

explanation: If community rules say women can only be examined by female staff, a lack of female doctors at the local clinic can cause a dangerous delay in treatment.

question: A patient who tested positive for a late-onset degenerative disorder expresses severe anxiety about the future and refuses to talk to family. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Provide a safe, empathetic space and offer referrals to counseling services
options.B: Urge the patient to quit their job and prepare for immediate full-time care
options.C: Tell the patient not to worry because symptoms might never appear
options.D: Contact the family members immediately to warn them about the gene

explanation: A supportive, non-judgmental approach combined with professional mental health referrals helps the patient process difficult emotional news at their own pace. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h5)

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community.

question: What is the main route of transmission for the pathogens that cause gastroenteritis?

options.A: Fecal-oral route
options.B: Broken skin contact
options.C: Direct droplet inhalation
options.D: Vector-borne mosquito bites

explanation: Gastroenteritis pathogens spread primarily when microscopic amounts of infected stool contaminate food, water, or hands and enter a new host's mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: A nurse is getting the tray ready for a sigmoidoscopy. Which tool is needed if the doctor wants to take a sample of a suspicious spot?

options.A: An IV infusion pump
options.B: A urinary catheter
options.C: A rigid speculum
options.D: Biopsy forceps

explanation: Awesome! Biopsy forceps slide right through the scope to pinch a tiny, painless tissue sample for the lab to check.

question: What is the biggest danger of pulling a Guinea worm out too fast?

options.A: The worm may snap, causing severe inflammation and infection
options.B: The patient will instantly lose consciousness from shock
options.C: The infection will immediately spread to other family members
options.D: The remaining worm will travel directly to the patient's heart

explanation: You nailed it! If the worm breaks, the leftover piece causes a nasty immune reaction and infection. Slow and steady wins the race in nursing procedures!

question: Why is recording a medication administration immediately after giving it so important?

options.A: It proves to the patient that the nurse is working efficiently
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to automatically restock the item
options.C: It prevents another nurse from accidentally giving the same dose
options.D: It satisfies hospital accreditation rules without clinical benefit

explanation: Prompt charting creates a clear real-time record that protects the patient from receiving a dangerous double dose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h1)

question: For a stroke patient with left-sided weakness who is confined to bed, what is the best nursing action to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Keeping the head of the bed completely flat at all times
options.B: Repositioning the patient every two hours and supporting weak limbs
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the skin dry
options.D: Massaging the reddened bony prominences vigorously every shift

explanation: You nailed it! Turning the patient regularly relieves pressure on vulnerable skin, while supporting weak limbs protects their joints.

question: What is the main problem that causes most cases of peripheral arterial disease (PAD)?

options.A: Deep veins staying stretched out permanently
options.B: Bacterial toxins destroying tiny capillaries
options.C: Tiny lymphatic tubes suddenly bursting
options.D: Fatty plaque building up and narrowing the arteries

explanation: That process is called atherosclerosis! Fat and cholesterol build up inside the arteries, making the pathway narrow so it's harder for oxygen-rich blood to reach the legs.

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of long-term rehabilitation after a nervous system injury?

options.A: Reversing the primary neural cell death caused by the initial crash
options.B: Helping the client adapt to permanent physical disabilities
options.C: Supporting family members through emotional counseling
options.D: Providing physical therapy to prevent muscle contractures

explanation: You nailed it! Once nerve cells die from the initial heavy impact, they don't grow back. Rehabilitation is all about maximizing the strength and independence the patient has left!

question: What must legally happen before a nurse can begin last offices?

options.A: Arrival of the mortuary attendants at the ward
options.B: Formal certification of death by a physician
options.C: Payment of all hospital bills by the family
options.D: Completion of the police report for the incident

explanation: A doctor must officially confirm and document death before any last offices or body transfers can take place. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: When would a nurse use an oropharyngeal airway device?

options.A: In an unconscious patient lacking gag reflexes
options.B: To suction mucus from a patient's stomach
options.C: To deliver oral medications for high blood pressure
options.D: In a conscious patient who is talking normally

explanation: These airways can make an awake patient vomit. We only use them on deeply unconscious patients who won't gag on it.

question: Which test is most helpful for checking acid-base balance after an asphyxial event?

options.A: Arterial blood gas analysis
options.B: Routine urinalysis dipstick
options.C: Serum electrolyte panel
options.D: Complete blood cell count

explanation: An ABG test is your best friend here. It gives you a direct look at the patient's blood pH, oxygen levels, and how well they are clearing out carbon dioxide.

question: What is the term for that exciting moment when a mother first feels the baby fluttering inside her womb?

options.A: Quickening
options.B: Balottement
options.C: Lightening
options.D: Engagement

explanation: Quickening is the mother feeling the baby move for the first time! It's a classic presumptive sign because only she can feel it.

question: What actually happens inside the body during a Type I allergic reaction to a medication?

options.A: Accumulation of fluid in the peripheral blood vessels
options.B: Mast cell degranulation releasing histamine and other mediators
options.C: Direct toxicity of the drug on the kidney tubules
options.D: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells in the liver

explanation: When antibodies trigger mast cells to burst open and release histamine, it leads to rapid itching, swelling, and trouble breathing.

question: Why is air injected into a closed medication vial before withdrawing the liquid?

options.A: To equalize pressure and make fluid withdrawal easier
options.B: To cool down the medication temperature inside the vial
options.C: To kill any bacteria that might be living in the drug
options.D: To dilute the medication before it enters the needle

explanation: Injecting air replaces the volume of liquid being removed, preventing a vacuum from forming inside the vial which makes drawing fluid difficult. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h5)

question: What must the doctor do after you report a suspected patient death?

options.A: Clean and prepare the patient room for a new admission
options.B: Notify the local news station about the patient condition
options.C: Immediately transport the body to the hospital mortuary
options.D: Perform an independent examination to formally certify death

explanation: Exactly! The doctor has to do their own check and sign the official papers.

question: Why do nurses perform multiple needle counts at different stages of one operation?

options.A: To follow hospital billing procedures for disposable items
options.B: To allow the surgeon time to review patient notes
options.C: To give the surgical team mandatory rest breaks
options.D: To catch and correct missing items before the wound is closed

explanation: Exactly! Checking at different milestones makes sure we catch any missing item while we can still easily find it. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is one of the biggest goals of home-based nursing care?

options.A: Reducing the need for any future medical checkups
options.B: Ensuring the patient moves permanently to a nursing home
options.C: Preventing unnecessary hospital readmissions
options.D: Eliminating the involvement of family members

explanation: Exactly! By managing health well at home, we keep patients comfortable and out of crowded hospital beds.

question: Why might a newly diagnosed patient temporarily use the defense mechanism of denial?

options.A: To protect the mind from overwhelming emotional pain
options.B: To increase their physical strength and immunity
options.C: To speed up cellular regeneration and wound healing
options.D: To permanently cure their underlying medical condition

explanation: Defense mechanisms like denial act as psychological buffers, shielding the individual from sudden, unbearable emotional shocks. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h3)

question: During which major conflicts did helicopters first become popular for rapid medical evacuation?

options.A: The American Civil War
options.B: World War I
options.C: The Korean and Vietnam Wars
options.D: World War II

explanation: Great job! Helicopters really changed wartime nursing during the Korean and Vietnam wars, helping nurses reach injured soldiers much closer to the front lines.

question: Why do hospitals prefer phased construction plans over shutting down completely during expansions?

options.A: They allow construction workers to finish the project in one day
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for architectural blueprints
options.C: They prevent the hospital from ever needing future maintenance
options.D: They minimize disruption to ongoing patient care services

explanation: Building section by section allows the hospital to keep its doors open, caring for patients safely while construction happens away from active wards.

question: What is the earliest physical sign of puberty in boys?

options.A: A sudden linear height spurt
options.B: Growth of facial hair
options.C: Deepening of the voice
options.D: Enlargement of the testes

explanation: Spot on! Testicular growth is the very first clinical sign that male puberty has begun.

question: What is the main focus of community-centred nursing care?

options.A: Promoting health within people's living environments
options.B: Conducting laboratory tests for rare diseases
options.C: Managing hospital emergency room admissions
options.D: Treating severe illnesses inside hospital wards

explanation: Community-centred care focuses on meeting people in their homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces to promote health rather than waiting for them to arrive at a hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of objective, professional nursing documentation?

options.A: Client is a difficult person who hates taking medications.
options.B: Client looks lazy and refuses to get out of bed.
options.C: Client cried during family visits and verbalized feeling hopeless.
options.D: Client is acting crazy and refusing to talk to anyone today.

explanation: Professional documentation records observable behaviors and direct client statements without personal judgment or bias. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h8)

question: Which of these is a known risk factor for developing severe menstrual cramps?

options.A: Living in a warm tropical climate
options.B: Starting menstrual periods at a very early age
options.C: Having a short duration of menstrual bleeding
options.D: Starting menstruation after age sixteen years

explanation: Correct! Early menarche (getting your period before age 11) is linked to a higher chance of primary dysmenorrhoea.

question: What is the main benefit of a spinal reflex loop like pulling your hand away from a hot stove?

options.A: It increases blood flow directly to the burned finger
options.B: It stores the memory of the hot stove permanently
options.C: It bypasses the brain to prevent delayed injury
options.D: It activates the hypothalamus to raise body temperature

explanation: Reflexes skip the time-consuming process of brain thinking, allowing lightning-fast muscle reactions to protect the body from harm. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h6)

question: A patient complains of a stubborn dry cough two weeks after starting a new blood pressure pill. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all medications immediately without telling anyone
options.B: Document the symptom and report it as a suspected adverse drug reaction
options.C: Ignore the complaint because coughs are unrelated to blood pressure drugs
options.D: Prescribe an over-the-counter cough syrup for the patient to use daily

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Always note down the change, discuss it with the team, and report it using the proper channels like the Yellow Form.

question: During which stage of pregnancy do the structures that form the fallopian tubes grow and fuse?

options.A: Near the end of the second trimester
options.B: During the first trimester
options.C: Throughout the third trimester
options.D: After birth during infancy

explanation: This happens very early in pregnancy—during the first trimester! Embryology can feel tricky, but you're mastering it step by step.

question: Approximately what percentage of a person's vulnerability to addiction is typically attributed to genetics?

options.A: Nearly 100 percent
options.B: Around 10 percent
options.C: About 50 percent
options.D: Less than 5 percent

explanation: Twin and family studies consistently show that genetic predisposition accounts for about half of a person's risk for developing an addiction. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the name of the delicate strip of skin on the underside of the penis that connects to the foreskin?

options.A: Corona
options.B: Preputial sac
options.C: Frenulum
options.D: Dorsal vein

explanation: Spot on! The frenulum is that sensitive little band of tissue underneath the penis. Surgeons take great care here because it has a rich blood supply.

question: Why do we recommend asking open-ended questions when discussing a serious diagnosis?

options.A: It forces the patient to give a short yes or no answer
options.B: It allows the nurse to finish the conversation much faster
options.C: It prevents the patient from asking difficult questions about dying
options.D: It helps the nurse understand the patient's current knowledge and perspective

explanation: Open-ended questions invite patients to share their thoughts in their own words, showing us how much they truly understand about their health. Excellent communication skill!

question: What is the main job of foetal circulation?

options.A: To supply oxygen and nutrients from the mother
options.B: To pump blood directly into the mother's kidneys
options.C: To circulate air through the baby's developing lungs
options.D: To filter all waste through the baby's own kidneys

explanation: You've got this! Since a baby in the womb cannot breathe air or eat food yet, the placenta steps in to bring oxygen and nutrients straight from the mother's blood. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Why is patient education important before discharge on a modified diet?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never need dental work again
options.B: It stops the patient from ever eating solid food
options.C: It helps family members prepare safe food textures at home
options.D: It replaces the need for follow-up doctor appointments

explanation: Educating patients and caregivers ensures they continue safe food preparation and know what to avoid after leaving the hospital. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical emotional response when a patient faces a permanent disability?

options.A: Grief over the loss of physical function
options.B: Anxiety about the future and financial strain
options.C: Depression due to lifestyle changes
options.D: Immediate and permanent acceptance without any sadness

explanation: Adapting to a disability is a complex emotional journey that usually involves shock, denial, and grief before acceptance is reached. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h7)

question: What generally happens to the tracheostomy hole (stoma) after the tube is permanently removed?

options.A: It requires major plastic surgery to sew shut
options.B: It naturally heals closed with a simple dressing
options.C: It must be plugged with a permanent metal cap
options.D: It remains permanently open for air passage

explanation: Nature is amazing! Covered with a simple dressing, the stoma usually shrinks and closes up on its own within a few days.

question: Why is recording baseline vital signs and functional ability on the initial assessment sheet important?

options.A: It proves to the family that the nurse arrived on time
options.B: It provides a starting point to measure future clinical progress or decline
options.C: It allows the nurse to discharge the client immediately on day one
options.D: It satisfies administrative paperwork without affecting daily nursing care

explanation: Baseline data gives the nurse a clear point of comparison to see if treatments are working or if the client's health is worsening. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: How should you document a normal deep tendon reflex score on a patient's chart?
explanation: On the reflex scale, 2+ is right in the sweet spot for a normal, average response.

question: What is a major hurdle when introducing telehealth gadgets to home care patients?

options.A: Internet access is legally banned in residential areas
options.B: Physicians refuse to look at remote monitoring data
options.C: Lack of digital literacy among patients and families
options.D: Telehealth devices completely eliminate all illnesses

explanation: Many patients—especially older adults—might feel intimidated by tablets or apps until you patiently walk them through it step by step.

question: Why do we track a child's growth over several visits rather than relying on just one measurement?

options.A: It prevents errors made by community health volunteers
options.B: It shows the direction and velocity of growth over time
options.C: It guarantees the child will not contract infectious diseases
options.D: It is required by government health insurance policies

explanation: A single visit only tells you about today. Tracking over time shows the true pattern—whether the child is growing well or falling behind.

question: Which ethical principle simply means the duty to do no harm to your patient?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Non-maleficence
options.C: Justice
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Non-maleficence is just a big word for a simple rule: do no harm. As a nurse, you always make sure your actions or mistakes don't cause unnecessary pain or suffering.

question: Which nursing diagnosis focuses directly on blood supply to the brain tissue?

options.A: Risk for Impaired Skin Integrity
options.B: Ineffective Tissue Perfusion (Cerebral)
options.C: Impaired Physical Mobility
options.D: Ineffective Airway Clearance

explanation: You've got this! This diagnosis simply points to situations where blood and oxygen aren't reaching brain cells properly because of swelling, clots, or bleeding.

question: A researcher studying a rare illness asks current patients to bring in friends or family members with the same condition. What is this called?

options.A: Quota sampling
options.B: Simple random sampling
options.C: Snowball sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: You got it! Just like a snowball rolling downhill gets bigger, participants help you recruit more participants from their network.

question: What is the golden rule when a nurse has to break tragic news of a death to family members?

options.A: Use clear, direct, and compassionate language
options.B: Ask another family member to break the news
options.C: Use complex medical terms to soften the blow
options.D: Delay the information until they stop crying

explanation: That's right! Being clear and direct avoids any confusion, ensuring the family understands the reality while feeling your compassion.

question: What is the main reason to gather all your equipment before positioning your patient?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory technician is present in the room
options.B: To prevent procedural delays and maintain a smooth workflow
options.C: To keep the examination table warm for the incoming patient
options.D: To fulfill mandatory legal requirements for waste disposal

explanation: Getting your tray ready beforehand means you won't have to leave a vulnerable patient alone while you run off to grab a missing item!

question: What is the primary purpose of a low protein diet?

options.A: To cure chronic infections in the urinary tract
options.B: To increase the speed of digestion in the stomach
options.C: To help the patient gain rapid muscle mass
options.D: To reduce the workload on organs that process waste

explanation: Limiting protein intake decreases the amount of nitrogen waste products that damaged organs must filter and clear from the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h1)

question: During an open irrigation, what must you do immediately after disconnecting the catheter and tubing?

options.A: Flush the drainage bag with hot tap water
options.B: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around
options.C: Clean the floor around the bed with bleach
options.D: Protect both exposed ends with sterile caps

explanation: Always keep it sterile! Covering those open tips stops stray germs from jumping onto the connectors and into your patient.

question: What causes an obstetric fistula when a young mother has a very long, difficult labor?

options.A: A sudden genetic weakness in the walls of the maternal bladder
options.B: Continuous pressure from the baby's head cutting off blood supply to soft tissues
options.C: Severe dehydration causing the kidneys to rupture during contractions
options.D: Direct surgical errors made by traditional birth attendants during delivery

explanation: When labor is blocked, the baby's head presses hard against the mother's soft tissues, cutting off blood flow. This causes tissue damage that forms an abnormal opening (fistula).

question: Why is it risky to rely solely on blood albumin levels to assess a sick patient's nutrition?

options.A: Albumin changes too slowly to be useful in a hospital setting.
options.B: Inflammation and fluid changes can alter albumin levels regardless of diet.
options.C: Blood tests for albumin are completely unreliable in all humans.
options.D: Albumin only measures how much water is inside the stomach.

explanation: Albumin is an acute-phase reactant; inflammation and fluid overload can lower its level even if the patient is well-nourished. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h6)

question: How many generations should a basic genetic pedigree chart ideally cover?

options.A: At least three generations
options.B: Five to seven generations
options.C: Only the immediate parents
options.D: Just the patient and their children

explanation: Mapping three generations helps reveal patterns of inheritance that might skip a generation or appear across multiple family members. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h2)

question: What is the basic medical definition of urinary incontinence?

options.A: The involuntary loss of urine
options.B: An infection in the urinary tract
options.C: Painful and burning urination
options.D: The complete inability to produce urine

explanation: Urinary incontinence specifically refers to the accidental or involuntary leaking of urine from the bladder. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is a major difference between standard examination gloves and surgical gloves?

options.A: Surgical gloves are strictly sterile and have longer cuffs
options.B: Examination gloves are always thicker and tougher
options.C: Examination gloves come in precise numbered hand sizes
options.D: Surgical gloves are only used for drawing blood

explanation: Surgical gloves are sterile and feature longer cuffs to cover your gown sleeves, keeping the operating field completely germ-free.

question: What is the main focus of geriatrics?

options.A: The social and economic policies affecting retirement
options.B: The medical care and treatment of older adults
options.C: The cellular biology of genetic mutations in youth
options.D: The psychological development of children and teens

explanation: Spot on! Geriatrics is simply the branch of healthcare that focuses on keeping older adults healthy and treating age-related conditions.

question: Why do nurses need to keep a close eye out when caring for women with sudden tummy pain in the emergency ward?

options.A: Patients may hide a history of unsafe abortion due to fear or legal stigma
options.B: Abortion complications never present with abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.C: Routine screening policies forbid nurses from asking about sexual history
options.D: Standard diagnostic tests cannot detect early stages of pregnancy

explanation: Fear of judgment or legal trouble often makes patients keep quiet about what really happened. As nurses, our compassionate detective work helps us uncover the truth and save lives!

question: What is a common long-term physical problem caused by having very heavy periods for a long time?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Broken bones
options.D: Severe adult asthma

explanation: You nailed it! Losing blood month after month empties out the body's iron reserves, leading directly to anemia.

question: What makes malaria an example of biological vector-borne transmission?

options.A: The mosquito only carries the parasite on the outside of its physical legs
options.B: The malaria parasite develops and multiplies inside the mosquito before being injected
options.C: The malaria pathogen is spread purely through human-to-human coughing
options.D: The disease can only live inside warm-blooded animal reservoirs

explanation: In biological transmission, the parasite undergoes a necessary part of its life cycle inside the vector before it can infect a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h6)

question: Used injection needles and surgical blades belong to which group of waste?

options.A: Sharps
options.B: General waste
options.C: Pharmaceutical waste
options.D: Pathological waste

explanation: Exactly! Any item that can cut or prick the skin, like needles and blades, is called a sharp.

question: A nursing student in a sterile gown accidentally lets their hands drop below their waist. What should they do?

options.A: Step back one foot and continue assisting the surgeon
options.B: Continue working because the gown is still clean on top
options.C: Acknowledge that sterility is broken and get a new gown
options.D: Ask the circulating nurse to wipe the gloves with alcohol

explanation: In theatre rules, anything below the waist is considered unsterile. Don't worry—accidents happen! Just step back, re-gown, and keep learning.

question: What does the word 'palsy' mean in relation to cerebral palsy?

options.A: Infection of the spinal cord
options.B: A sudden loss of consciousness
options.C: Weakness or problems using muscles
options.D: Gradual shrinking of the brain

explanation: Palsy specifically refers to a lack of muscle control or weakness that interferes with normal movement. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is it important to use local languages and traditional communication channels for immunization campaigns?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on printed books
options.B: It is required to qualify for international medical grants
options.C: It stops people from visiting traditional bone setters
options.D: It ensures the message is clearly understood and trusted by residents

explanation: Using familiar languages and traditional methods like town criers breaks down communication barriers and reduces fear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h3)

question: What is a top public health strategy for preventing neural tube defects?

options.A: Folic acid supplements before and during early pregnancy
options.B: Avoiding all exercise during childbearing years
options.C: Giving routine antibiotics to all newborns
options.D: Mandatory bed rest in the third trimester

explanation: Spreading the word about folic acid before and during early pregnancy is a proven lifesaver that prevents neural tube issues on a massive scale.

question: A patient with a head injury seems stable. Why must you keep monitoring them closely over the next few days?

options.A: Complications often develop hours or days after the primary injury
options.B: Hospital policies require discharges within 48 hours
options.C: Patients usually fake their symptoms to get more attention
options.D: Medications stop working completely after the first day

explanation: Brain swelling takes time to build up. A patient looking fine right now can take a sudden turn for the worse later, so constant watch is key!

question: What is the main chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) released at parasympathetic target organs?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key messenger used by the parasympathetic system to talk to target organs. You're building a strong foundation in pharmacology and physiology!

question: What is a major benefit of continuous antenatal risk assessment?

options.A: Complete prevention of all natural labor pains
options.B: Early detection of potential complications before labor starts
options.C: Guaranteeing that the baby will be born on a specific day
options.D: Removing the need for traditional birth attendants entirely

explanation: Catching warning signs early allows the healthcare team to act before a minor issue becomes an emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h2)

question: What happens to the arterioles in your muscles when you start heavy exercise?

options.A: They collapse completely to stop bleeding
options.B: They harden permanently to boost pressure
options.C: They dilate to let more blood through
options.D: They constrict to block fast blood flow

explanation: Working muscles need more oxygen, so local arterioles relax and open wide to increase blood supply. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: You realize you forgot to document a vital medication given two hours ago. What should you do?

options.A: Leave it out entirely because late charting is illegal
options.B: Write a late entry clearly labeled with the current time and the actual time of the event
options.C: Wait until the end of the month and add it to the file
options.D: Squeeze the note between previous lines and backdate your signature

explanation: Spot on! Always write a clear 'late entry' with the correct times. Never backdate or try to squeeze notes between lines.

question: Why is standing up slowly from a bed or chair especially important for patients with balance issues?

options.A: It ensures that the inner ear fluid drains out of the ear canal completely
options.B: It allows the heart rate to drop safely before physical exertion begins
options.C: It prevents permanent muscle cramps in the lower extremities
options.D: It gives the nervous system time to adjust and prevents sudden vertigo or dizziness

explanation: Moving too fast can trigger a sudden dizzy spell (vertigo) or a drop in blood pressure. Taking it slow keeps our patients safe and steady on their feet!

question: Which blood protein acts like a sponge to hold fluid inside the blood vessels?

options.A: Globulin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Fibrinogen

explanation: Great job! Albumin creates what we call oncotic pressure—think of it as a magnet pulling fluid back into the bloodstream so it doesn't leak out into the tissues.
